messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@titanpay.com>

Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spike — transactions failing

Sofia,

We're seeing a sustained latency spike across inference calls to Redwood for the fraud-score model over the last 15 minutes. Error rates have climbed to ~8% and tail latency is >3s on our production path — several transaction batches are timing out. This is impacting payment authorization (volume impacted: ~120 TPS at peak).

Attached are truncated pcap/logs from our side (titan-logs-0214.zip). Our engineers are on standby but requested you escalate immediately — this is affecting live users and settlement windows.

Can you confirm you see the same metrics on your side and advise immediate mitigation/rollback options? We need an ETA for stabilization.

— Elena

Subject: Re: Production latency spike — transactions failing

Thanks for flagging, Elena — I see correlated errors and elevated p99 on our telemetry (fraud-score-runner). I'm escalating to an exec war-room and starting immediate mitigations. Initial notes:

- Scope: customer-facing inference path for TitanPay (model: fraud-score-v3).
- Symptoms: elevated p95/p99, increased 5xx from inference gateway, queue buildup on GPU pool.
- Immediate mitigation plan (in progress):
  1) Force-fallback routing to dedicated high-throughput pool (if capacity permits).
  2) Temporarily scale dedicated concurrency + enable lighter quantized variant (fraud-score-v3-q4) for non-critical flows.
  3) Enable short TTL KV cache priming for recurring prefixes.

Marissa — please spin up a war-room (exec invite) and include runbook. Vivek/Jonas — triage kernel/driver errors and check node-level OOMs. Connor — liaise with TitanPay SRE for any client-side timeouts.

I'll keep Elena updated every 30 mins.

— Sofia

Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 08:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — quick triage

Quick triage from infra:
- Observed spikes in preemptible eviction rates on the low-latency pool servicing TitanPay around 08:05 PST; several pods restarted due to driver-level GPU memory pressure.
- Model v3 has a larger KV working set and we've seen KV cache churn.

Short-term mitigations applied (08:30):
- Routed 60% of traffic to high-throughput pool (rebalanced requests).
- Decreased per-request beam size and pinned v3-q4 for non-auth flows.

Expected impact: should lower tail latency in ~10–15 mins. If OOMs continue, recommend full traffic diversion to a warm dedicated pool and a rolling restart of affected nodes (risk: brief request dropping).

Need decision on whether to offer a temporary credits/discount if TitanPay experiences revenue loss during mitigation.

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

- Mitigations applied at 08:30 PST (routing + model fallback) have reduced p95 by ~40% and decreased error rate to ~1.5%. Throughput still ~10–15% below baseline during peak.

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 02:05:00 -08:00
Subject: TitanPay incident — stabilization & next steps

Elena / TitanPay team — final update:

Summary:
- Root cause: accelerated KV cache churn combined with a recent driver update that increased memory pressure on a subset of our low-latency nodes.
- Impact window: 2027-02-14T08:05 to 2027-02-14T13:02 PST (partial degradation until warm pool drain completed).
- Customer impact: increased p99 and ~6% total authorization retries; estimated revenue exposure is under review with TitanPay.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: traffic diverted to warm dedicated pool; rolled back driver on affected nodes; enabled quantized model fallback for high-latency paths.
- Remediation: scheduled targeted kernel/driver patch and improved KV cache eviction heuristics.
- Postmortem: we will publish a joint postmortem within 72 hours and include telemetry, timeline, and remediation checklist.

Commercial: we recognize the disruption. Sofia will coordinate a commercial offer (credit or fee waiver) and a follow-up exec review with TitanPay.

If there are any urgent questions before the postmortem, flag them here and we'll prioritize. Thanks to the TitanPay team for rapid collaboration.

— Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
